subject: Interlock: GPU slice fair-share matrix and soft reserve proposal
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@vertexcloud.com>, Tom Brooks <t.brooks@nimbus.health>
Date: Sat, 14 Jun 2025 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Interlock: GPU slice fair-share matrix and soft reserve proposal

Team —

We have two pilot customers (Nimbus Health + VertexCloud) requesting predictable burst capacity in Q3. Ops asked us to formalize a "fair-share matrix" for GPU slices so we can:

- Allocate soft reserves (non-binding buffers) for pilots without hard eviction in the first 30 days
- Define prioritization when pools are contended (latency SLO, paid reserved lanes, trial pilots)

Attached is an initial spreadsheet (fairshare-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a short proposal PDF outlining a two-tier soft-reserve approach. High-level asks:

1) Product: sign off on prioritization dimensions (latency class, paid commit, pilot stage, regulatory needs)
2) Finance: confirm whether we can offer soft-reserve credits for Nimbus Health as part of DEAL-8473
3) Ops: confirm feasibility of implementing soft reserves as a policy flag (eviction grace window + telemetry alerts)

Milestone: need a cross-functional alignment call next week so we can commit slice reservations by 2025-06-23.

Notes for context: Nimbus expects a 3x spike for a 48h ingestion run mid-July; VertexCloud is evaluating a dedicated lane for inference latency-sensitive traffic.

Thanks —
Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: fairshare-matrix-v1.xlsx; slice-soft-reserve-proposal.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@vertexcloud.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interlock: GPU slice fair-share matrix and soft reserve proposal

Thanks Markus — good initiative. A few quick clarifying questions before I sign off:

- Prioritization dimensions: do we treat SLA-backed dedicated customers above pilot soft-reserve customers in all contention scenarios? That will change the matrix logic.
- Soft reserve enforcement: is this a preference-only flag (best-effort) or do you want hard token accounting with temporary quota bump mechanics?
- Default grace window: proposal shows 30 days. We should consider a 14-day initial window with the option to extend for approved pilots to reduce long tail blocking.

From a product roadmap standpoint, implementing a non-trivial prioritization engine is a Q3 effort if it requires new routing decisions. If we keep it as a metadata-driven filter (policy tags + eviction weight), we can ship configuration controls this quarter.

Can Ops/Aditya confirm complexity and rough ETA? If Ops needs more time, propose an interim manual carve-out workflow that CS can manage for high-value pilots.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Operations

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Brooks <t.brooks@nimbus.health>
Date: Mon, 16 Jun 2025 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interlock: GPU slice fair-share matrix and soft reserve proposal

Quick ops readout:

- Feasibility: implementing a soft-reserve flag that adjusts eviction weight is doable without a full routing rewrite. We'll add an eviction_weight field that biases packer/eviction decisions.
- Complexity: low to medium. Requires: policy -> scheduler mapping; dashboard to surface active soft reserves; alerting when a reserve is evicted. Estimated engineering effort: ~3 sprints if we include dashboarding; 1 sprint for backend flag + scheduler change.
- Implementation suggestion: implement as metadata-driven "soft_reserve" boolean + "reserve_ttl_days" integer. Default to 14 days; allow CS to request extensions with an audit log.

Operational caveat: this will not prevent hard preemption for critical infra incidents. We should document edge-case behavior in the runbook.

Attachment: usage-samples.pdf (sample telemetry showing spike patterns for Nimbus).

—Aditya (Infra/Platform)

From: Tom Brooks <t.brooks@nimbus.health>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Interlock: GPU slice fair-share matrix and soft reserve proposal

Appreciate the heads-up, team. From Nimbus's side:

- The July ingestion is non-negotiable; we need low eviction risk for a 48h window. A soft reserve with clear SLA fallback and an option to convert to a short-term paid reservation (48h) would work.
- We can agree to an audit window and provide a short-term payment to secure a burst lane if required.

If you can provide a simple API/console flow for me or my ops contact to request a short-term reservation (and accept a one-time fee), we can use that instead of asking for permanent quota changes.

—Tom Brooks
Head of ML Infrastructure, Nimbus Health

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@vertexcloud.com>, Tom Brooks <t.brooks@nimbus.health>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interlock: GPU slice fair-share matrix and soft reserve proposal

Thanks everyone — alignment notes and next steps:

- Product decision: Kimberly approves metadata-driven approach (soft_reserve boolean + reserve_ttl_days) with default 14 days.
- Ops plan: Aditya to ship backend flag + scheduler change in 1 sprint; dashboarding and alerts over next 2 sprints. Runbook will explicitly state emergency preemption rules.
- Commercial/Finance: Monica to propose a one-time burst fee for 48h paid reservations and include a credit option for Nimbus under DEAL-8473.
- Customer flow: Marcos (CS) to add a manual request flow in the Console for now; we will evaluate automating a public API in Q3.

Action owners:
- Aditya: implement backend flag, ETA 2025-07-05 (start of sprint).
- Monica: draft billing proposal and credit mechanics by 2025-06-20.
- Markus: coordinate pilot communications and confirm Nimbus willingness to accept short-term paid burst if necessary.
- Kimberly: finalize product doc and quickstart for CS by 2025-06-22.

I'll schedule a 30-minute interlock on 2025-06-19 to walk through the runbook and billing path. If anybody has objections to the default 14-day window, speak up before EOD 2025-06-19.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachments included: slice-soft-reserve-proposal.pdf (updated)
